summary: The note surveys ten school-based mental health initiatives launched between September 2023 and January 2024 at different schools. They include mindfulness sessions, peer support networks, mental health days, on-demand counseling, emotional literacy workshops, collaborative art, therapy animals, wellness clubs, Safe Talk Time and awareness weeks. The common principle is that mental health is integral to overall well-being and educational success.
one_line: Ten school programs launched in 2023-2024 that support student mental health, from mindfulness and peer support to therapy animals and awareness weeks.
key_facts: Madison Elementary introduced mindfulness and meditation on October 15, 2023, led by school counselor Julia Mendez, with 10 minutes each morning dedicated to the practices.
Lincoln High School has had student-led peer support networks since November 3, 2023, led by sociology teacher Mark Thomson; anonymized feedback helps staff tailor support services.
Principal Laura Gibson of Harrison Middle School advocates mental health days, launched December 10, 2023, which let students recharge without stigma or academic penalties.
Jefferson High launched the "Counselor Connect" program on January 6, 2024, offering walk-in or appointment counseling led by school psychologist Dr. Nathan Hargreaves, which reduced wait times.
Roosevelt Junior High has run emotional literacy workshops since September 15, 2023, with a curriculum developed by emotional development expert Dr. Samantha Clark.

Wilson Elementary School's Art-for-the-Heart program, started September 22, 2023 and pioneered by art teacher Elena Rodriguez, has students contribute to collaborative art pieces as a non-verbal way to express shared emotions.
Grant High School introduced therapy dogs and other comforting animals on September 29, 2023 to reduce student stress and anxiety.
Adams Vocational High School launched wellness clubs, ranging from yoga to nutrition-based societies, on October 8, 2023, as proposed by health teacher Kevin Lopez.
Patterson Charter School's Safe Talk Time, initiated by Vice Principal Amy Young since November 18, 2023, schedules moderated, informal periods for open discussion without fear of judgment.

Baker Technical Institute has held an annual Mental Health Awareness Week since its first event on October 20, 2023, organized by the student council and guidance counselors with speakers, workshops and exhibits.
The note states that all ten initiatives share the principle that mental health is integral to overall well-being and educational success.
